title: HB1098 (2021 Regular): Civil Liability For Extreme Risk Protection Orders

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Colorado) (gun-policy Stage 5, Colorado); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Colorado text (Introduced (02/16/2021), 2021-02-16; official copy, https://content.leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/documents/2021A/bills/2021a_1098_01.pdf)
provenance.note: Introduced version 02/16/2021 (as filed); the record shows no passage vote, so later amendments, if any, are not in the text read. Section 1 legislative declaration (claims the ERPO law violates the U.S. Constitution) is not quoted.

operative_text:
Section 2 (C.R.S. 13-21-133(1)): A PERSON OR A PERSONAL REPRESENTATIVE OF A PERSON WHO SUFFERS INJURY OR DAMAGES AS A RESULT OF NOT BEING ABLE TO USE A FIREARM TO DEFEND HIMSELF, HERSELF, OR HIS OR HER FAMILY AS A RESULT OF A TEMPORARY EXTREME RISK PROTECTION ORDER ISSUED PURSUANT TO SECTION 13-14.5-103 OR AN ONGOING EXTREME RISK PROTECTION ORDER ISSUED PURSUANT TO SECTION 13-14.5-104 MAY BRING A CIVIL ACTION TO RECOVER DAMAGES AGAINST ANY PERSON WHO DRAFTED, PROPOSED, PROMOTED, OR PROVIDED SUPPORT, FINANCIAL OR OTHERWISE, TO PASS, IMPLEMENT, OR ENFORCE HOUSE BILL 19-1177.
Section 2 (C.R.S. 13-21-133(2)): A PLAINTIFF WHO PREVAILS IN AN ACTION PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION IS ENTITLED TO REASONABLE ATTORNEY FEES AND EITHER: (a) ALL DAMAGES REASONABLY NECESSARY TO COMPENSATE THE PLAINTIFF FOR ANY PHYSICAL, PSYCHOLOGICAL, OR EMOTIONAL INJURIES, INCLUDING POST-TRAUMATIC STRESS DISORDER, SUFFERED AS A RESULT OF NOT BEING ABLE TO USE A FIREARM TO DEFEND HIMSELF OR HERSELF; OR (b) LIQUIDATED DAMAGES OF AT LEAST ONE HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS OR UP TO ONE HUNDRED MILLION DOLLARS IF DEATH OR DISABILITY OCCURS.
